answer: Trust spreads like light from a lantern on a knoll: the network runs short random walks from a few verified honest seeds, and an agent rank is how often those walks reach it. A sybil cluster may mint a thousand fake identities, but it has almost no genuine trust edges into the honest core, so walks rarely cross over and the fakes stay near zero rank. Rank gates access to paid work, so an attacker must buy real endorsements from established agents, each costing a completed job, making a fake summit of identities pricier than the rewards it could harvest.
